meta.installaties-en-keuringen.html.titl: Installations and inspections for hotels · Lemnion
meta.installaties-en-keuringen.html.desc: Which periodic inspections apply to the installations in your hotel? From the SCIOS scopes for electrical installations and solar panels to gas lines. We list the inspection obligations.
installaties.sub: On top of energy performance requirements, there are periodic inspections for the installations in your hotel: electrical systems, heating boilers, solar panels and charging infrastructure. We explain which scopes exist, what is legally required and how often an inspection is needed.
installaties.wat-p: The term scope comes from the SCIOS certification scheme, the recognised inspection methodology for periodic installation checks. It is not a legal term. The legal basis is the employer's duty of care under the Working Conditions Act (Article 3) and the requirement to have your workplace inspected regularly (Working Conditions Decree, Article 3.2). A SCIOS inspection is the generally accepted way to demonstrate that you comply.
installaties.wie-h2: Which scopes apply to your hotel?
installaties.wie-lead: SCIOS distinguishes scopes for combustion and electrical installations. These are the scopes most relevant to a hotel.
installaties.c1p: Periodic inspection of your electrical installation: the distribution board, cables, protection and permanently connected equipment, in line with NEN 3140.
installaties.c2p: Electrical work equipment in and around the building, such as the equipment your staff use daily.
installaties.c3p: PV panels, inverter and connection. Relevant if you generate your own solar power.
installaties.c4p: Inspection of the heating systems in the building, alongside and separate from the statutory energy performance requirements.
installaties.c5p: Heating boilers: atmospheric, with forced draught burner, and steam or hot water boilers.
installaties.c6p: Fuel lines for gas. Relevant as long as your building runs on gas.
installaties.freq-p: There is no fixed statutory inspection frequency that requires you to be inspected every set number of years. How often an inspection is needed depends on the risk and follows from your risk assessment (RI&E) and the interval guidelines of NEN 3140. In practice this ranges from annually to once every 1 to 3 years for higher risk and up to about 5 years for low risk. Many insurers do make such an inspection contractually mandatory for business premises.
installaties.opslag-h2: Battery and charging infrastructure fall under the electrical scope
installaties.opslag-p: EV charging infrastructure and stationary battery storage are fixed electrical installations. They therefore fall under Scope 8 and the periodic inspection under NEN 3140. In addition, NEN 1010 applies to new installations or extensions. Solar panels fall under Scope 12. For the specific fire safety of stationary lithium storage, the PGS 37 guideline applies: a safety code rather than an inspection scope.
installaties.apart-h2: Different from the energy performance obligations
installaties.apart-p: The statutory EPBD and EED inspection obligation for heating and air-conditioning systems, including the BACS (GACS) obligation, is a separate system without scope numbers. Within the SCIOS world, Scope 14 is the closest inspection of building heating systems. We keep separate for you which obligation concerns what.
installaties.ctah: Want to know which inspections apply to your hotel?
installaties.ctap: In a short conversation we map which inspections are running or needed and how to align them with your energy plans. No strings attached.
